content.title: About
content.content: Parsnip is a root vegetable from the Apiaceae family, related to carrots. It has a creamy color, a sweet‑nutty flavor, and a crisp texture. Raw parsnip is often used in salads, pickles, and as a crunchy addition to dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Parsnip was popular in medieval Europe when carrots were mainly purple.
Sugar content increases during storage, making the root sweeter over time.
Compared with carrots, parsnip contains more fiber and minerals such as potassium and magnesium.
Raw parsnip can be grated on a coarse grater and added to salads as a carrot substitute.
In some countries parsnip is called "white carrot" because of its similar taste.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Parsnip provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, helps maintain satiety, and regulates blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal heart and muscle function and helps maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Parsnip is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to parsnip, manifested as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Foodborne contamination
items.content: Raw root vegetables can be contaminated with bacteria or nitrates, so they should be washed thoroughly before eating.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw parsnip may cause gas and discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw parsnip can be sliced thin, grated on a coarse grater, or cut into matchsticks for salads, pickles, and sandwiches. It also works well on vegetable platters with dip sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store parsnips in the refrigerator in a sealed bag or container, where they stay fresh for up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, wrap the roots in a damp towel to prevent drying out.
